latin: Venatio illa Socratis, de qua in Protagora, conuenienter per sex gradus potest sic distribui: ut primus sit esse materiae extrinsecae, secundus esse particulare immateriale, tertius esse uniuersale, quartus esse rationale, quintus esse particulare intellectuale, sextus esse totale intellectuale; in septimo tanquam, in sabbato, cessandum est a uenatione.
latin_note: 1486 print has minor punctuation variants ('immateriale.Tertius'); 1487 reads 'potest sic describi' and 'tanquam sabbato' (farmer1998:23219-23220); wording otherwise unchanged.
translation: Socrates's hunt in the Protagoras divides neatly into six stages: first, the being of matter outside us; second, particular immaterial being; third, universal being; fourth, rational being; fifth, particular intellectual being; sixth, total intellectual being—after which, in a seventh stage, as on the Sabbath, the hunt must stop.
